author: Tyler Hill
title: Civic Club gives away almost 100-thousand dollars to victims of July storms - NewsBreak
text:
By Tyler Hill No media credit provided. ,
2 hours ago
TEUTOPOLIS, Ill. (WCIA) — After severe weather touched down nearly one month ago, people in Teutopolis say they knew something needed to be done. So, a charity organization in the village reached out to community members and they stepped up in– a generous way
Jerry Runde–the treasurer for the Teutopolis Civic Club says the biggest eye-opener was visiting the property of coworkers and friends. And seeing all of this devastation firsthand.
He says others in the club had similar experiences. And they wanted to be able to help meet big needs. Through word of mouth and social media—they collected money through donations grants, and cash the organization already had set aside. Tally it all up and they’ve given away more than $93,000 in a little less than four weeks.
“It’s a couple times now, two times in three years with the anhydrous accident and now with this tornado. The same thing three years ago. Community just rallies. They’re here to help. They’ll do what they need to. I guess we’re just here to facilitate.” said Runde.
Runde says they’ve received checks from Indiana — Kentucky — and Florida. All from former residents seeing this devastation — and responding with kindness.
He says the Civic Club is still looking to meet needs. If you would like to donate you can reach out to them here or send it to P.O. Box 93, Teutopolis, IL., 62467.
